incidents.title: SyRI welfare fraud-detection system halted by court
incidents.summary: The District Court of The Hague ruled the SyRI legislation (Systeem Risico Indicatie) unlawful for breaching Article 8 ECHR: the opaque, inter-agency data-linkage risk model targeted low-income neighbourhoods and lacked sufficient safeguards, with a risk of discrimination by socio-economic and migration background. The system was halted.
incidents.notes: Judgment: District Court of The Hague, ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2020:865 (English ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2020:1878).

incidents.title: Clearview AI — untargeted scraping of facial images in France
incidents.summary: CNIL order (MED-2021-134, 26 November 2021, made public 6 December 2021) finding Clearview AI unlawfully collected and processed facial images of people in France without a legal basis to build a facial-recognition database sold to law enforcement.
incidents.notes: Order of 26 November 2021, made public 6 December 2021.

incidents.title: ChatGPT data breach exposing users' conversations and payment data
incidents.summary: On 20 March 2023 a ChatGPT bug exposed other users' chat histories and partial payment details; the breach was cited by the Garante in its 31 March 2023 action against OpenAI, alongside the absence of a legal basis for training-data collection and of age verification.
incidents.source_title: Garante, 31 Mar 2023: Artificial intelligence: stop to ChatGPT by the Italian SA
incidents.notes: Breach cited by the Garante in its 31 March 2023 action against OpenAI.

incidents.title: Grok sexualised deepfakes disseminated on X
incidents.summary: The Commission found the risks of Grok's functionalities deployed into X "seem to have materialised", with manipulated sexually explicit images — including content that may amount to child sexual abuse material — disseminated in the EU, exposing citizens to serious harm.

responses.actor: Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL)
responses.summary: CNIL's restricted committee imposed the then-maximum GDPR fine of €20m on Clearview AI for unlawful biometric processing, failure to honour access/erasure rights and non-cooperation, ordered it to stop collecting French residents' data and delete what it held within two months, under a €100,000/day penalty. Announced 20 October 2022.
responses.notes: Fine announced 20 October 2022; €100,000/day penalty for non-compliance. The CNIL's own press-release page for the sanction is no longer published (named decisions are delisted after the publicity period), so the decision text is linked via Légifrance.

responses.summary: The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens fined the Minister of Finance/Tax Administration €3.7m for the Fraude Signalering Voorziening (FSV), a blacklist holding fraud signals on over 270,000 people (2013–2020) with no legal basis, inaccurate/outdated data, excessive retention and inadequate security. Decision 7 April 2022, published 12 April 2022.
responses.source_title: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, 12 Apr 2022: Boete Belastingdienst voor zwarte lijst FSV
responses.notes: Decision of 7 April 2022, published 12 April 2022. No single incident row: the FSV blacklist ran 2013–2020 and no verified incident date was established. The full fine decision is linked under 'Publicaties' on the AP page.

responses.actor: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
responses.summary: The Garante imposed an urgent temporary limitation on Luka Inc.'s processing of Italian users' data via the Replika AI companion chatbot, finding concrete risks to minors (sexually inappropriate replies, no age verification) and no valid legal basis for processing children's data.
responses.source_title: Garante, 3 Feb 2023: Artificial intelligence: italian SA clamps down on 'Replika' chatbot
responses.notes: Urgent temporary limitation on Luka Inc.'s processing of Italian users' data via Replika.

responses.actor: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
responses.summary: The Garante ordered an immediate temporary limitation on OpenAI's processing of Italians' personal data via ChatGPT (provision of 30 March 2023, announced 31 March), citing no legal basis for mass training-data collection, no user information, inaccurate outputs and no age verification; the Garante set conditions on 12 April 2023 for lifting the limitation; service resumed 28 April 2023.
responses.source_title: Garante, 31 Mar 2023: Artificial intelligence: stop to ChatGPT by the Italian SA
responses.notes: Provision of 30 March 2023, announced 31 March; the Garante set conditions on 12 April 2023 for lifting the limitation (OpenAI to comply by 30 April); service resumed 28 April 2023.

responses.summary: The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens imposed a €30.5m fine on Clearview AI (decision 16 May 2024, announced 3 September 2024) for its illegal facial-recognition database of 30bn+ photos including Dutch citizens, plus an order subject to a penalty of up to €5.1m for continued non-compliance; it is also examining personal liability of directors.
responses.notes: Decision of 16 May 2024, announced 3 September 2024. Not linked to FR-I-01: that incident is the French CNIL finding; the Dutch fine concerns Clearview's database including Dutch citizens.

responses.summary: Report of the EDPB ChatGPT Taskforce (established 13 April 2023) setting out preliminary views on lawfulness, fairness, accuracy, transparency and data-subject rights for ChatGPT, including that web-scraped training data poses fundamental-rights risks and that compliance responsibility cannot be transferred to data subjects.
responses.source_title: European Data Protection Board, ChatGPT Taskforce report

responses.summary: The DPC concluded High Court proceedings (brought 8 August 2024 under s.134 Data Protection Act 2018) after X agreed permanently to adhere to its undertaking on processing EU/EEA users' public posts to train Grok; the DPC had warned of risks to fundamental rights, and simultaneously asked the EDPB for the Art. 64(2) opinion that became Opinion 28/2024.
responses.notes: High Court proceedings brought 8 August 2024 under s.134 Data Protection Act 2018. Not linked to EU-I-01: these proceedings concerned Grok training, not the 2026 deepfakes.

responses.actor: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
responses.summary: The Garante ordered an urgent, immediate limitation on Hangzhou and Beijing DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence's processing of Italian users' data and opened an investigation, after the companies' reply to its 28 January information request was judged "completely insufficient" and they claimed EU law did not apply to them; the order also cited storage of data in China without GDPR safeguards.
responses.source_title: Garante, 30 Jan 2025: Artificial Intelligence: The Italian Data Protection Authority blocks DeepSeek
responses.notes: Urgent limitation on Hangzhou and Beijing DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence; investigation opened.

responses.summary: The Commission opened new formal DSA proceedings against X and extended its December 2023 proceedings, to assess whether X diligently assessed and mitigated systemic risks from deploying Grok into X (including illegal content, gender-based violence and harm to physical/mental well-being) and filed the required ad hoc risk assessment; suspected infringements of DSA Arts. 34, 35 and 42.
responses.notes: Formal DSA proceedings opened; suspected infringements of DSA Arts. 34, 35 and 42. Binding 'no': proceedings are an investigation, not a final decision.

instruments.title: General Data Protection Regulation — Regulation (EU) 2016/679
instruments.summary: The EU's general data-protection law, published in the OJ on 4 May 2016 and applicable from 25 May 2018; Arts. 5, 6, 9, 22 and 35 are the main GDPR hooks used against AI training, profiling and automated decision-making.

instruments.title: Digital Services Act — Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
instruments.summary: Sets due-diligence, content-moderation and systemic-risk duties for online intermediaries and very large online platforms; published in the OJ on 27 October 2022, applicable from 17 February 2024. It is the legal basis for the Commission's DSA proceedings against X/Grok.

instruments.title: European AI Office established — Commission Decision C/2024/1459
instruments.summary: Establishes the European AI Office within DG CNECT to implement and enforce the AI Act, especially the rules for general-purpose AI models. Decision of 24 January 2024, published in the OJ on 14 February 2024, in force 21 February 2024.
instruments.notes: Decision of 24 January 2024, published in the OJ on 14 February 2024.

instruments.title: EU AI Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
instruments.summary: The world's first comprehensive AI law: risk-based rules for AI systems, prohibitions, high-risk obligations, GPAI duties and transparency duties. Adopted 13 June 2024, published in the OJ on 12 July 2024, in force 1 August 2024.
instruments.next_milestone: 2 Dec 2027: high-risk duties begin (Annex III stand-alone systems)

instruments.title: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 on AI models and personal data
instruments.summary: EDPB opinion (requested by the Irish DPC) on when an AI model trained on personal data can be considered anonymous, when legitimate interest is a lawful basis for training/deployment, and the consequences of unlawful training data.

instruments.title: Commission Guidelines on prohibited AI practices (Art. 5 AI Act)
instruments.summary: Non-binding Commission guidelines interpreting the eight prohibited AI practices (manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, crime-risk prediction, untargeted facial scraping, emotion recognition, biometric categorisation, real-time remote biometric identification). The prohibitions applied from 2 February 2025.
instruments.source_title: European Commission, Guidelines on prohibited AI practices (C(2025) 884 final, published 4 Feb 2025; formally adopted as C(2025) 5052 final, 29 Jul 2025)
instruments.notes: The prohibitions applied from 2 February 2025. Content approved 4 Feb 2025 as C(2025) 884 final; formally adopted 29 Jul 2025 as C(2025) 5052 final.

instruments.title: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
instruments.summary: Voluntary code drawn up by 13 independent experts with ~1,000 stakeholders, in three chapters (Transparency, Copyright, Safety and Security), to help GPAI providers demonstrate compliance with Arts. 53 and 55 AI Act. Confirmed by the Commission and AI Board as an adequate voluntary compliance tool.
instruments.notes: Drawn up by 13 independent experts with ~1,000 stakeholders; three chapters (Transparency, Copyright, Safety and Security).

instruments.title: Digital Omnibus on AI — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
instruments.summary: Amends the AI Act to simplify implementation: postpones high-risk application dates (2 Dec 2027 for stand-alone Annex III systems; 2 Aug 2028 for Annex I product-embedded systems), narrows some duties, and adds two new prohibited practices (Art. 5(1)(ba)–(bb)): AI systems generating non-consensual intimate material and child sexual abuse material, applicable from 2 Dec 2026. Published in the OJ 24 July 2026, in force 27 July 2026.
instruments.next_milestone: 2 Dec 2026: new Art. 5 prohibitions (ba)–(bb) apply; 2 Dec 2027: high-risk duties begin (Annex III stand-alone systems); 2 Aug 2028: Annex I product-embedded systems

instruments.title: France — National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Launched March 2018 following the Villani report; €1,527m public funding for 2018–2022 across research, higher education, public transformation, economy and defence/security, with an acceleration phase announced November 2021 for 2022–2025.
instruments.source_title: Ministère de l'Économie, Stratégie nationale pour l'IA, 2e phase — dossier de presse, 8 Nov 2021
instruments.notes: Following the Villani report; €1,527m public funding for 2018–2022; acceleration phase announced November 2021 for 2022–2025.

instruments.title: Germany — AI Strategy of the Federal Government
instruments.summary: Federal strategy adopted 15 November 2018 and updated 2 December 2020, aiming for competitive, human-centric and trustworthy "AI made in Germany"; initial €3bn to 2025, raised to ~€5bn in the 2020 update, which added pandemic, sustainability and health priorities.
instruments.source_title: Die Bundesregierung, Strategie Künstliche Intelligenz — Fortschreibung 2020 (Dec 2020)
instruments.notes: Updated 2 December 2020; initial €3bn to 2025, raised to ~€5bn in the 2020 update.

instruments.title: Denmark — National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Government strategy (Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industry, Business and Financial Affairs), March 2019, aiming to make Denmark a front-runner in responsible AI use, with four objectives (ethical human-centric basis, research, business growth, world-class public services) and 24 initiatives.

instruments.title: Netherlands — Strategic Action Plan for Artificial Intelligence (SAPAI)
instruments.summary: Government of the Netherlands action plan built on three pillars: capitalising on societal/economic opportunities, creating the right conditions (education, research, data, connectivity), and strengthening foundations (public values, human rights, trust and safety).
instruments.source_title: Tweede Kamer, Parliamentary Papers blg-903667 (SAPAI report)

instruments.title: Poland — Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland from 2020
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers Resolution No. 196 of 28 December 2020 (Monitor Polski 2021, item 23) setting short-, medium- and long-term AI goals across six areas: society, innovative companies, science, education, international cooperation and the public sector.
instruments.notes: Council of Ministers Resolution No. 196 of 28 December 2020.

instruments.title: Ireland — National AI Strategy, "AI – Here for Good"
instruments.summary: Ireland's first national AI strategy, launched 8 July 2021 by the Taoiseach and the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment; a whole-of-government roadmap for trustworthy, human-centric AI adoption in enterprise and public services, refreshed in November 2024.

instruments.title: Spain — AESIA created, Royal Decree 729/2023
instruments.summary: Royal Decree 729/2023 of 22 August 2023 approves the statute of the Agencia Española de Supervisión de la Inteligencia Artificial (AESIA), based in A Coruña — the first EU member-state AI supervision agency, later Spain's AI market-surveillance authority and single point of contact. Published in the BOE on 2 September 2023.
instruments.notes: Published in the BOE on 2 September 2023; based in A Coruña; Spain's AI market-surveillance authority and single point of contact.

instruments.title: Spain — Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers approval on 14 May 2024 of the updated AI strategy (continuing the 2020 ENIA), structured in three axes and eight levers — supercomputing, Spanish/co-official-language models (ALIA), public- and private-sector uptake, and transparent, ethical, humanistic AI — with €1.5bn for 2024–2025.

instruments.title: Italy — AI Law, Legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132
instruments.summary: Italy's comprehensive national AI law ("Disposizioni e deleghe al Governo in materia di intelligenza artificiale"), the first such law in the EU; it sets a biennial national AI strategy, designates AgID and the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) as national AI authorities, and adds AI-related criminal offences. Published in Gazzetta Ufficiale No. 223 on 25 September 2025, in force 10 October 2025.
instruments.notes: First comprehensive national AI law in the EU; in force 10 October 2025.

changelog.change: Version 0.1: first release with 4 incidents, 9 responses and 17 instruments across the EU and 8 member states. Every row has a source link and a confidence rating.
Fixed NL-P-01 source link: the Rijksoverheid policy-note URL is dead (404), replaced with the official parliamentary publication of the SAPAI report (Tweede Kamer blg-903667). No data changed.

Audit and compliance fixes: Garante rows IT-I-01, IT-R-01, IT-R-02, IT-R-03 now cite the specific releases (not the press-room index); IT-R-02 corrected — the Garante set conditions on 12 Apr 2023 for lifting the ChatGPT limitation, service resumed 28 Apr 2023; FR-R-01 now cites the CNIL sanction decision (SAN-2022-019, via Légifrance) with LINC kept as an additional source; NL-R-01 now cites the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens decision page; EU-P-06, DE-P-01 and FR-P-01 now cite the specific guideline/strategy documents; EU-P-08 corrected to two new Art. 5 prohibitions (ba)–(bb) applicable from 2 Dec 2026. events.title: Grok image-generation misuse and EU response
events.summary: Image-editing features on Grok, built into X, were used from late December 2025 to create non-consensual sexualised edits of real people, including minors. The European Commission opened DSA proceedings on 26 January 2026.
events.caution: The onset date is the start of a documented analysis window of mass misuse; sources differ on the exact start, so day counts are approximate.
events.regional_note: EU-level action: the Commission's DSA proceedings (IP/26/203) opened 26 January 2026; the Irish DPC had already concluded separate Grok training proceedings in September 2024.
